sample_context: Geographically diverse low-passage and laboratory strains
finding: Maximum nucleotide divergence between nearly complete genomes was 0.4%; newly generated sequences were closer to SD90e than HG52.
implication_for_project: Supports broad conservation while warning that HG52 alone is not a representative population reference.
source_title: Genome Sequencing and Analysis of Geographically Diverse Clinical Isolates of Herpes Simplex Virus 2

sample_context: Genital lesion swabs from 38 people across three continents
finding: The study found 1,468 intragenic substitutions; maximum concatenated UL/US nucleotide distance was 0.4%, and even the most variable proteins had nonsynonymous changes in less than 3% of amino acids.
implication_for_project: Provides an independent clinical-sample benchmark for the convenience strain panel and protein-conservation estimates.
source_title: Highly conserved intragenic HSV-2 sequences: Results from next-generation sequencing of HSV-2 UL and US regions from genital swabs collected from 3 continents

sample_context: Retrospective clinical-isolate screen for a divergent HSV-2 variant
finding: Fourteen HSV-2 variant isolates were identified (2.8%); the variant lineage showed substantially greater UL30 diversity than classical HSV-2.
implication_for_project: Shows that high average conservation can hide lineage-specific guide escape risk in UL30 and motivates held-out lineage testing.
source_title: Genetic Diversity within Alphaherpesviruses: Characterization of a Novel Variant of Herpes Simplex Virus 2

sample_context: Thirty-six clinical strains plus HG52 typed in a 400-bp UL53 region
finding: The UL53 region contained multiple polymorphic sites and separated the clinical strains into 16 sequence groups.
implication_for_project: Shows that gene-level local entropy can be higher than the genome-wide average and should be evaluated at each candidate coordinate.
source_title: Discrimination of Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 Strains by Nucleotide Sequence Variations
